statement: One line holds l and r. Print how many primes lie in the inclusive range l to r. Sieve once up to r, then prefix-sum the flags: cnt(x) counts primes up to x, and the answer is cnt(r) minus cnt(l - 1) - one subtraction, reusable across any number of queries. Respect the bottom edge: 1 is no prime (one divisor), 2 is (the only even one), and l may be as low as 1.
constraints: A single sieve to r suffices.

example.why: 11, 13, 17 and 19 are prime; 15 is 3 times 5 and the evens fall to 2.

hint: Prefix counts turn the boolean array into an any-range answer machine.
mistake: Counting 1 as prime when l is 1 - the sieve must excuse 0 and 1 before any marking begins.
